claim: gdf3 is expressed maternally and ubiquitously during early stages of zebrafish development.
source: gdf3 is expressed maternally and ubiquitously during early stages of zebrafish development (Figure 1A) (Helde and Grunwald, 1993).
evidence: Supported by Figure 1A showing expression patterns and citation to Helde and Grunwald, 1993

claim: The amount of gdf3 mRNA diminishes rapidly through the blastula and gastrula stages and disappears by approximately 90% epiboly.
source: The amount of gdf3 mRNA diminishes rapidly through the blastula and gastrula stages and disappears by approximately 90% epiboly (Helde and Grunwald, 1993).
evidence: Supported by citation to Helde and Grunwald, 1993

claim: gdf3 expression returns in a tissue-restricted manner starting at the late bud stage and progressing into somitogenesis, when expression is observed in the lateral plate mesoderm (LPM) and in cells around KV.
source: This is followed by the return of expression in a tissue-restricted manner starting at the late bud stage and progressing into somitogenesis, when expression is observed in the lateral plate mesoderm (LPM) and in cells around KV (Figure 1A) (Peterson et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by Figure 1A and citation to Peterson et al., 2013

claim: Three mutant alleles of gdf3 (pr05, pr06, pr11) contain premature stop codons in the first exon, prior to the mature ligand domain-encoding region.
source: Each of the three mutant alleles contained a premature stop codon in the first exon, prior to the mature ligand domain-encoding region, and are thus predicted to be null alleles.
evidence: Described in the text and shown in Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1

claim: The three gdf3 mutant alleles are predicted to be null alleles.
source: Each of the three mutant alleles contained a premature stop codon in the first exon, prior to the mature ligand domain-encoding region, and are thus predicted to be null alleles.
evidence: Based on the presence of premature stop codons before the functional domain

claim: Homozygous gdf3 zygotic mutant embryos (Zgdf3) displayed no gross morphological phenotypes and were indistinguishable from heterozygous controls.
source: Homozygous gdf3 zygotic mutant embryos (Zgdf3) displayed no gross morphological phenotypes, were indistinguishable from heterozygous controls (Figure 1C and D), and grew to adulthood.
evidence: Supported by observations and Figure 1C and D

claim: Homozygous gdf3 zygotic mutant embryos grew to adulthood.
source: Homozygous gdf3 zygotic mutant embryos (Zgdf3) displayed no gross morphological phenotypes, were indistinguishable from heterozygous controls (Figure 1C and D), and grew to adulthood.
evidence: Direct observation reported in the text

claim: Embryos lacking maternal gdf3 (Mgdf3) displayed overt developmental defects.
source: By contrast, embryos lacking maternal gdf3 (Mgdf3) displayed overt developmental defects (Figure 1E) and did not survive beyond 3 days post fertilization (dpf).
evidence: Supported by observations and Figure 1E

claim: Embryos lacking maternal gdf3 (Mgdf3) did not survive beyond 3 days post fertilization (dpf).
source: By contrast, embryos lacking maternal gdf3 (Mgdf3) displayed overt developmental defects (Figure 1E) and did not survive beyond 3 days post fertilization (dpf).
evidence: Direct observation reported in the text

claim: Mgdf3 and maternal-zygotic gdf3 (MZgdf3) embryos were indistinguishable from each other.
source: Mgdf3 and maternal-zygotic gdf3 (MZgdf3) embryos were indistinguishable from each other (Figure 1E and F), suggesting that the loss of Zgdf3 did not contribute further to the gross Mgdf3 phenotype.
evidence: Supported by observations and Figure 1E and F

claim: The loss of zygotic gdf3 did not contribute further to the gross Mgdf3 phenotype.
source: Mgdf3 and maternal-zygotic gdf3 (MZgdf3) embryos were indistinguishable from each other (Figure 1E and F), suggesting that the loss of Zgdf3 did not contribute further to the gross Mgdf3 phenotype.
evidence: Inferred from the indistinguishability of Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos

claim: The defects in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos could be rescued with wild-type gdf3 mRNA.
source: Moreover, these defects could be rescued with wild-type (WT) gdf3 mRNA (Figure 1G and H), a result that confirms the mutant phenotypes arose from disruption of the gdf3 locus.
evidence: Supported by rescue experiments shown in Figure 1G and H

claim: The mutant phenotypes in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos arose from disruption of the gdf3 locus.
source: Moreover, these defects could be rescued with wild-type (WT) gdf3 mRNA (Figure 1G and H), a result that confirms the mutant phenotypes arose from disruption of the gdf3 locus.
evidence: Confirmed by rescue experiments with wild-type gdf3 mRNA

claim: The defects in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos strongly resemble the phenotypes exhibited by double mutants for the zebrafish Nodal orthologs ndr1 and ndr2.
source: The defects in Mgdf3 and in MZgdf3 embryos strongly resemble the phenotypes exhibited by double mutants for the zebrafish Nodal orthlogs ndr1 and ndr2 (Feldman et al., 1998) and MZ mutants for the essential Nodal co-receptor, teratocarcinoma-derived growth factor 1 (tdgf1; previously known as one eyed pinhead) (Gritsman et al., 1999).
evidence: Comparison to published phenotypes from Feldman et al., 1998

claim: The defects in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos strongly resemble the phenotypes exhibited by MZ mutants for the essential Nodal co-receptor tdgf1.
source: The defects in Mgdf3 and in MZgdf3 embryos strongly resemble the phenotypes exhibited by double mutants for the zebrafish Nodal orthlogs ndr1 and ndr2 (Feldman et al., 1998) and MZ mutants for the essential Nodal co-receptor, teratocarcinoma-derived growth factor 1 (tdgf1; previously known as one eyed pinhead) (Gritsman et al., 1999).
evidence: Comparison to published phenotypes from Gritsman et al., 1999

claim: Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos exhibit dorsal accumulation of cells following convergence and epiboly at the tailbud stage.
source: Similarities include the dorsal accumulation of cells following convergence and epiboly in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos at the tailbud stage, displacing the anterior most region of these embryos vegetally by 90 degrees compared to WT embryos (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E and F; compare to embryos in Gritsman et al., 1999).
evidence: Supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 2E and F

claim: Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos at 26 hours post fertilization (hpf) are cyclopic.
source: Additionally, Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos at 26 hours post fertilization (hpf) are cyclopic and exhibit extensive defects in mesoderm and endoderm formation (Figure 1E and F and below), again reminiscent of ndr1;ndr2 double mutants and MZtdgf1 mutants (Feldman et al., 1998; Gritsman et al., 1999).
evidence: Supported by observations and Figure 1E and F

claim: Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos at 26 hpf exhibit extensive defects in mesoderm and endoderm formation.
source: Additionally, Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos at 26 hours post fertilization (hpf) are cyclopic and exhibit extensive defects in mesoderm and endoderm formation (Figure 1E and F and below), again reminiscent of ndr1;ndr2 double mutants and MZtdgf1 mutants (Feldman et al., 1998; Gritsman et al., 1999).
evidence: Supported by observations and Figure 1E and F

claim: Maternally-supplied gdf3 is required for early embryogenesis.
source: Thus, maternally-supplied gdf3 is required for early embryogenesis, and loss of function cause defects that are consistent with strong reduction of early Nodal signaling.
evidence: Inferred from the severe developmental defects in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos

claim: Loss of gdf3 function causes defects that are consistent with strong reduction of early Nodal signaling.
source: Thus, maternally-supplied gdf3 is required for early embryogenesis, and loss of function cause defects that are consistent with strong reduction of early Nodal signaling.
evidence: Inferred from similarity to Nodal mutant phenotypes

claim: The Nodal target gene lefty1 (lft1) was absent in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos.
source: The Nodal target gene lefty1 (lft1) was absent in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: Supported by RNA in situ hybridization shown in Figure 2A–C

claim: Expression of ndr2 initiated in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos but was expressed at lower levels compared with controls.
source: While expression of ndr2 initiated in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos, it was expressed at lower levels compared with controls (Figure 2D–F); since Nodal signals propagate ndr2 expression, this result and the absence of lft1 suggests that Nodal signaling is markedly reduced or lost in the absence of maternal gdf3.
evidence: Supported by RNA in situ hybridization shown in Figure 2D–F

claim: Nodal signaling is markedly reduced or lost in the absence of maternal gdf3.
source: While expression of ndr2 initiated in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos, it was expressed at lower levels compared with controls (Figure 2D–F); since Nodal signals propagate ndr2 expression, this result and the absence of lft1 suggests that Nodal signaling is markedly reduced or lost in the absence of maternal gdf3.
evidence: Inferred from reduced ndr2 expression and absence of lft1

claim: goosecoid (gsc) is absent in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos.
source: goosecoid (gsc) (Stachel et al., 1993), a marker of progenitors of the prechordal plate, is absent in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos (Figure 2G–I).
evidence: Supported by RNA in situ hybridization shown in Figure 2G–I

claim: Expression of floating head (flh) is decreased in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos.
source: Expression of floating head (flh) (Talbot et al., 1995), a Nodal target that marks notochord progenitors (Gritsman et al., 2000), is decreased in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos (Figure 2J and K).
evidence: Supported by RNA in situ hybridization shown in Figure 2J and K

claim: Expression of no tail (ntl) in the dorsal region is absent in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos.
source: Similarly, expression of no tail (ntl) in the dorsal region (Schulte-Merker et al., 1992), a domain that requires the highest levels of Nodal signaling (Gritsman et al., 2000), is absent in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos (Figure 2L and M).
evidence: Supported by RNA in situ hybridization shown in Figure 2L and M

claim: axial (axl) was absent in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos.
source: axial (axl) (Strähle et al., 1993), a marker of progenitors of axial mesoderm and endoderm, and sox17 (Alexander and Stainier, 1999), a marker of presumptive endoderm, were both absent in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos (Figure 2N–Q).
evidence: Supported by RNA in situ hybridization shown in Figure 2N–Q

claim: sox17 was absent in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos.
source: axial (axl) (Strähle et al., 1993), a marker of progenitors of axial mesoderm and endoderm, and sox17 (Alexander and Stainier, 1999), a marker of presumptive endoderm, were both absent in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos (Figure 2N–Q).
evidence: Supported by RNA in situ hybridization shown in Figure 2N–Q

claim: Nodal signaling is strongly diminished or absent in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 mutants.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that Nodal signaling is strongly diminished or absent in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 mutants and, as a result, mesoderm and endoderm are not induced.
evidence: Inferred from the absence or reduction of multiple Nodal target genes

claim: Mesoderm and endoderm are not induced in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 mutants.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that Nodal signaling is strongly diminished or absent in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 mutants and, as a result, mesoderm and endoderm are not induced.
evidence: Inferred from the absence of mesendoderm markers

claim: Injection of gdf3 mRNA into MZgdf3 embryos at the one-cell stage led to the recovery of gsc expression.
source: To confirm that these effects on Nodal target genes were a result of the loss of Gdf3, we injected gdf3 mRNA into MZgdf3 embryos at the one-cell stage. This led to the recovery of gsc (Figure 2R and S), lft1, ntl, and sox17 expression, (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–F) confirming the role of gdf3 in regulating Nodal target genes.
evidence: Supported by rescue experiments shown in Figure 2R and S

claim: Injection of gdf3 mRNA into MZgdf3 embryos at the one-cell stage led to the recovery of lft1, ntl, and sox17 expression.
source: To confirm that these effects on Nodal target genes were a result of the loss of Gdf3, we injected gdf3 mRNA into MZgdf3 embryos at the one-cell stage. This led to the recovery of gsc (Figure 2R and S), lft1, ntl, and sox17 expression, (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–F) confirming the role of gdf3 in regulating Nodal target genes.
evidence: Supported by rescue experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–F

claim: gdf3 plays a role in regulating Nodal target genes.
source: To confirm that these effects on Nodal target genes were a result of the loss of Gdf3, we injected gdf3 mRNA into MZgdf3 embryos at the one-cell stage. This led to the recovery of gsc (Figure 2R and S), lft1, ntl, and sox17 expression, (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–F) confirming the role of gdf3 in regulating Nodal target genes.
evidence: Confirmed by rescue experiments restoring Nodal target gene expression

claim: Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 mutants consistently exhibit longer tails than ndr1:ndr2 double mutants.
source: While Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 mutants strongly resemble ndr1:ndr2 double mutants, Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos consistently exhibit longer tails.
evidence: Direct observation comparing mutant phenotypes

claim: The tail phenotype of Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos resembles that of MZfoxh1p1r/pr1 mutants.
source: This phenotype resembles that of MZfoxh1p1r/pr1 mutants in which a subset of Nodal signaling is eliminated by loss of the Foxh1 transcription factor, but signaling through other Nodal-activated transcription factors is retained (Slagle et al., 2011).
evidence: Comparison to published phenotypes from Slagle et al., 2011

claim: Injection of ndr1:ndr2 MOs into MZgdf3 mutants led to a tail defect that closely resembled the tail of ndr1:ndr2 double morphants.
source: Injection of the ndr1:ndr2 MOs into MZgdf3 mutants led to a tail defect that closely resembled the tail of ndr1:ndr2 double morphants (Figure 3A and B) and ndr1:ndr2 double mutants (Feldman et al., 1998).
evidence: Supported by morpholino knockdown experiments shown in Figure 3A and B

claim: 1 pg of ndr1 led to a modest expansion of gsc expression in WT embryos.
source: Although 1 pg of ndr1 led to a modest expansion of gsc expression in WT embryos (Figure 3C and D), it did not activate gsc expression in MZgdf3 embryos (Figure 3F and G).
evidence: Supported by overexpression experiments shown in Figure 3C and D

claim: 1 pg of ndr1 did not activate gsc expression in MZgdf3 embryos.
source: Although 1 pg of ndr1 led to a modest expansion of gsc expression in WT embryos (Figure 3C and D), it did not activate gsc expression in MZgdf3 embryos (Figure 3F and G).
evidence: Supported by overexpression experiments shown in Figure 3F and G

claim: 10 pg of injected ndr1 mRNA led to broad gsc expression in both WT and MZgdf3 mutant embryos.
source: By contrast, 10 pg of injected ndr1 mRNA led to broad gsc expression in both WT and MZgdf3 mutant embryos (Figure 3E and H).
evidence: Supported by overexpression experiments shown in Figure 3E and H

claim: There is residual low-level Nodal activity present in the Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 mutant embryos that is inadequate for the formation of head and trunk endoderm.
source: These data, combined with our marker gene expression analysis, suggests that there is residual low-level Nodal activity present in the Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 mutant embryos that is inadequate for the formation of head and trunk endoderm.
evidence: Inferred from the presence of tail structures and requirement for high Nodal levels to activate gsc

claim: At 70% epiboly, a ventral-to-dorsal increase in p-Smad1/5/8 was observed in MZgdf3 mutants compared to controls, with the ventral end exhibiting the largest increase in phosphorylation.
source: At 70% epiboly, a ventral-to-dorsal increase in p-Smad1/5/8 was observed in MZgdf3 mutants compared to controls, with the ventral end exhibiting the largest increase in phosphorylation (Figure 3I and J).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3I and J

claim: An expansion in expression of the Bmp target and ventral mesoderm marker eve1 towards the dorsal side of the embryo was observed in MZgdf3 mutants.
source: Consequently, we observed an expansion in expression of the Bmp target and ventral mesoderm marker eve1 (Joly et al., 1993) towards the dorsal side of the embryo (Figure 3K–M).
evidence: Supported by RNA in situ hybridization shown in Figure 3K–M

claim: Gdf3 plays a role in modulating Bmp signaling and restricting the expansion of the ventral mesoderm.
source: These data suggest that Gdf3 plays a role in modulating Bmp signaling and restricting the expansion of the ventral mesoderm.
evidence: Inferred from increased Bmp signaling and expanded eve1 expression in MZgdf3 mutants

claim: Dorsal expression of the Bmp inhibitor chordin (chd) is decreased in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos.
source: We also note that dorsal expression of the Bmp inhibitor chordin (chd) (Figure 3N–Q) is decreased in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos; this would also allow for the increased Bmp signaling observed in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos.
evidence: Supported by RNA in situ hybridization shown in Figure 3N–Q

claim: Decreased chordin expression would allow for the increased Bmp signaling observed in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos.
source: We also note that dorsal expression of the Bmp inhibitor chordin (chd) (Figure 3N–Q) is decreased in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos; this would also allow for the increased Bmp signaling observed in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos.
evidence: Inferred from the role of chordin as a Bmp inhibitor

claim: MO knockdown of Gdf3 reduces the expression of the nodal ortholog spaw in the LPM.
source: Gdf3 is also required for Nodal signaling in the LPM, since MO knockdown of Gdf3 reduces the expression of the nodal ortholog spaw in this tissue (Figure 4A) (Peterson et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by morpholino knockdown experiments shown in Figure 4A and citation to Peterson et al., 2013

claim: Zgdf3 mutants did not exhibit defects in the laterality of heart jogging.
source: Therefore, we expected L-R patterning defects in our mutants. However, Zgdf3 mutants did not exhibit defects in the laterality of heart jogging (data not shown), an asymmetric morphogenetic event that acts as a measure of L-R patterning (Baker et al., 2008; Smith et al., 2008; de Campos-Baptista et al., 2008).
evidence: Direct observation reported in the text

claim: Gdf3 is a stable protein that remains detectable in the zebrafish embryo as late as 2.5 dpf, well beyond stages of reported mRNA expression.
source: Gdf3 is a stable protein since it remains detectable in the zebrafish embryo as late as 2.5 dpf, well beyond stages of reported mRNA expression (Helde and Grunwald, 1993; Dohrmann et al., 1996).
evidence: Supported by citations to Helde and Grunwald, 1993 and Dohrmann et al., 1996

claim: In the absence of zygotic Gdf3, maternally supplied Gdf3 might compensate in L-R patterning events.
source: In the absence of zygotic Gdf3, maternally supplied Gdf3 might compensate in L-R patterning events.
evidence: Speculation based on protein stability and lack of phenotype in Zgdf3 mutants

claim: The anterior-posterior asymmetry in cell morphology in Kupffer's vesicle is lost in gdf3 morphants.
source: Immunostaining of aPKC (white) and GFP driven by the sox17 regulatory region (green) in Kupffer's Vesicle (KV) at 10 ss. The anterior-posterior asymmetry in cell morphology is lost in gdf3 morphants. Cells are outlined by white dashed lines.
evidence: Supported by immunostaining shown in Figure 4B

claim: Attenuation of maternal Gdf3 leads to improper cell morphology during KV development.
source: KV development is aberrant in MO-injected embryos. Normally, the cells in the anterior-dorsal region of KV are columnar and more tightly packed as compared to the ventral region (Figure 4B, see uninjected). This architecture is proposed to generate left-ward asymmetric flow that is faster across the anterior-dorsal portion of KV (Prabhat et al., 2007; Okabe et al., 2008; Supatto et al., 2008; Wang et al., 2012; Grimes and Burdine, 2017). In Gdf3 knockdowns, this architecture is lost and all the cells exhibited a cuboidal morphology (Figure 4B, see gdf3 MO).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining shown in Figure 4B

claim: Gdf3 knockdown can adversely affect the formation of KV, which would prevent the generation of normal asymmetric fluid flow.
source: These data demonstrate that Gdf3 knockdown can adversely affect the formation of KV, which would prevent the generation of normal asymmetric fluid flow.
evidence: Inferred from the loss of proper KV cell architecture in gdf3 morphants

claim: Gdf3 knockdowns expressed dand5 symmetrically in contrast to WT embryos which exhibit a right-biased expression of dand5.
source: In contrast to WT embryos which exhibit a right-biased expression of dand5, Gdf3 knockdowns expressed dand5 symmetrically (Figure 4C).
evidence: Supported by RNA in situ hybridization shown in Figure 4C

claim: Coinjection of ntla MO did not restore spaw expression in the LPM of gdf3 morphants.
source: We found that coinjection of ntla MO did not restore spaw expression in the LPM of gdf3 morphants (Figure 4D).
evidence: Supported by double morpholino knockdown experiments shown in Figure 4D

claim: Gdf3 is required for robust Spaw signaling, and without Gdf3, Spaw is unable to induce its own expression, even in the absence of midline-derived Spaw inhibitors.
source: This suggests that Gdf3 is required for robust Spaw signaling, and without Gdf3, Spaw is unable to induce its own expression, even in the absence of midline-derived Spaw inhibitors.
evidence: Inferred from the failure to restore spaw expression in gdf3+ntla double morphants

claim: Injection of 50 pg of gdf3 mRNA in Mgdf3 embryos rescued mesendoderm formation and resulted in ~90% of embryos with normal L-R patterning based on the direction of heart jogging.
source: Injection of 50 pg of gdf3 mRNA in Mgdf3 embryos, which retain zygotic expression of gdf3, rescued mesendoderm formation and resulted in ~90% of embryos with normal L-R patterning based on the direction of heart jogging (Figure 5A).
evidence: Supported by rescue experiments shown in Figure 5A

claim: Injection of 50 pg of gdf3 mRNA in MZgdf3 embryos rescued mesendoderm defects but these embryos exhibited defects in heart jogging laterality, with ~50% of hearts jogging incorrectly to the right or remaining midline.
source: Injection of 50 pg of gdf3 mRNA in MZgdf3 embryos also rescued mesendoderm defects but these embryos exhibited defects in heart jogging laterality, with ~50% of hearts jogging incorrectly to the right or remaining midline (Figure 5A).
evidence: Supported by rescue experiments shown in Figure 5A

claim: Zygotic gdf3 facilitates left-right patterning in the absence of sufficient maternal gdf3 contribution.
source: These data suggest that zygotic gdf3 facilitates left-right patterning in the absence of sufficient maternal gdf3 contribution.
evidence: Inferred from the difference in L-R patterning rescue between Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos

claim: Zygotic Gdf3 is not required for L-R patterning in the presence of maternal Gdf3.
source: However, since Zgdf3 mutants exhibit no L-R defects, zygotic Gdf3 is not required for L-R patterning in the presence of maternal Gdf3.
evidence: Inferred from the lack of L-R phenotypes in Zgdf3 mutants

claim: Injecting increasing amounts of gdf3 mRNA increased the number of MZgdf3 embryos with correct leftward jogged hearts.
source: In further support of the hypothesis that Gdf3 produced early in development is stable and sufficient to function in L-R patterning, injecting increasing amounts of gdf3 mRNA increased the number of MZgdf3 embryos with correct leftward jogged hearts (Figure 5A).
evidence: Supported by dose-response rescue experiments shown in Figure 5A

claim: Gdf3 produced early in development is stable and sufficient to function in L-R patterning.
source: In further support of the hypothesis that Gdf3 produced early in development is stable and sufficient to function in L-R patterning, injecting increasing amounts of gdf3 mRNA increased the number of MZgdf3 embryos with correct leftward jogged hearts (Figure 5A).
evidence: Supported by dose-response rescue experiments

claim: Presence of LPM and expression of spaw in the LPM is rescued in M/MZgdf3 mutant embryos injected with gdf3 mRNA.
source: While the LPM does not form in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos, presence of LPM and expression of spaw in the LPM is rescued in mutant embryos injected with gdf3 mRNA (Figure 5B).
evidence: Supported by rescue experiments shown in Figure 5B

claim: In injected MZgdf3 embryos, LPM spaw laterality was irregular with ~40% of embryos displaying correct left-sided expression at the 12 somite stage.
source: In injected MZgdf3 embryos, LPM spaw laterality was irregular with ~40% of embryos displaying correct left-sided expression at the 12 somite stage (ss).
evidence: Quantification of spaw expression patterns in rescue experiments

claim: In injected Mgdf3 embryos, where zygotic gdf3 is still present, the number of embryos exhibiting correct left-sided expression of spaw increased to ~70%.
source: In injected Mgdf3 embryos, where zygotic gdf3 is still present, the number of embryos exhibiting correct left-sided expression of spaw increased to ~70%.
evidence: Quantification of spaw expression patterns in rescue experiments

claim: Zygotic gdf3 contributes to correct L-R patterning in the absence of maternal Gdf3.
source: This further supports the conclusion that zygotic gdf3 contributes to correct L-R patterning in the absence of maternal Gdf3.
evidence: Inferred from the improved spaw laterality in Mgdf3 vs MZgdf3 rescue experiments

claim: Correct asymmetric dand5 expression in KV was restored in rescued Mgdf3 embryos.
source: While correct asymmetric dand5 expression in KV was restored in rescued Mgdf3 embryos (Figure 5C and H–I), rescued MZgdf3 embryos expressed dand5 symmetrically (Figure 5C and F–G), indicating loss of functional flow in KV, likely owing to aberrant KV morphology.
evidence: Supported by RNA in situ hybridization shown in Figure 5C and H–I

claim: Rescued MZgdf3 embryos expressed dand5 symmetrically, indicating loss of functional flow in KV, likely owing to aberrant KV morphology.
source: While correct asymmetric dand5 expression in KV was restored in rescued Mgdf3 embryos (Figure 5C and H–I), rescued MZgdf3 embryos expressed dand5 symmetrically (Figure 5C and F–G), indicating loss of functional flow in KV, likely owing to aberrant KV morphology.
evidence: Supported by RNA in situ hybridization shown in Figure 5C and F–G

claim: Zygotic Gdf3 is required for proper formation and function of KV in the absence of maternal Gdf3.
source: These data suggest that zygotic Gdf3 is required for proper formation and function of KV in the absence of maternal Gdf3.
evidence: Inferred from the difference in dand5 expression patterns between rescued Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos

claim: gdf3 is a maternal effect gene for early embryonic patterning.
source: Here, we show that the gene encoding the Vg1 ortholog in zebrafish, gdf3, is a maternal effect gene for early embryonic patterning.
evidence: Conclusion based on the severe phenotypes in Mgdf3 but not Zgdf3 mutants

claim: The role of maternally supplied Gdf3 is to promote robust levels of Nodal signaling.
source: We provide evidence that the role of maternally supplied Gdf3 is to promote robust levels of Nodal signaling.
evidence: Conclusion based on the reduction of Nodal target genes in Mgdf3/MZgdf3 mutants

claim: Nodal and Vg1 orthologs can bind to one another.
source: Others have reported that Nodal and Vg1 orthologs can bind to one another (Tanaka et al., 2007; Fuerer et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Tanaka et al., 2007 and Fuerer et al., 2014

claim: Vg1 requires the same pathway components as Nodal ligands for signaling, including the essential co-receptor Tdgf1.
source: Furthermore, Vg1 requires the same pathway components as Nodal ligands for signaling, including the essential co-receptor Tdgf1 (Cheng et al., 2003).
evidence: Supported by citation to Cheng et al., 2003

claim: Gdf3 dimerizes with Nodal to facilitate Nodal signaling during development.
source: Thus, we hypothesize that Gdf3 dimerizes with Nodal to facilitate Nodal signaling during development.
evidence: Hypothesis based on evidence of Nodal-Vg1 binding and shared pathway components

claim: Lower levels of Nodal signaling still occur in the absence of maternal Gdf3.
source: Our evidence suggests that lower levels of Nodal signaling still occur in the absence of maternal Gdf3.
evidence: Inferred from the presence of tail structures and residual Nodal activity in Mgdf3/MZgdf3 mutants

claim: Nodal can signal independently of Gdf3.
source: Although Nodal can signal independently of Gdf3, target genes required for head and trunk mesendoderm are not activated without Gdf3 unless Nodal is overexpressed beyond physiological levels.
evidence: Inferred from the ability of high levels of Nodal to activate gsc in MZgdf3 mutants

claim: Target genes required for head and trunk mesendoderm are not activated without Gdf3 unless Nodal is overexpressed beyond physiological levels.
source: Although Nodal can signal independently of Gdf3, target genes required for head and trunk mesendoderm are not activated without Gdf3 unless Nodal is overexpressed beyond physiological levels.
evidence: Supported by experiments showing gsc activation only with high Nodal levels in MZgdf3 mutants

claim: Correct spatial expression of mesendoderm marker genes occurs in MZgdf3 embryos injected with gdf3 mRNA.
source: Moreover, we find correct spatial expression of mesendoderm marker genes in MZgdf3 embryos injected with gdf3 mRNA, which suggests that Gdf3 plays a permissive role in mesendoderm formation while spatial restriction of ndr1 and ndr2 expression is critical for patterning.
evidence: Observed in rescue experiments

claim: Gdf3 plays a permissive role in mesendoderm formation while spatial restriction of ndr1 and ndr2 expression is critical for patterning.
source: Moreover, we find correct spatial expression of mesendoderm marker genes in MZgdf3 embryos injected with gdf3 mRNA, which suggests that Gdf3 plays a permissive role in mesendoderm formation while spatial restriction of ndr1 and ndr2 expression is critical for patterning.
evidence: Inferred from the correct spatial expression of markers in rescued embryos

claim: An increase in Bmp signaling is observed in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos by assaying for pSMAD1/5/8.
source: Gdf3 has also been proposed to act as a direct inhibitor of Bmp signaling (Birsoy et al., 2006; Levine and Brivanlou, 2006), and we observe an increase in Bmp signaling in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos by assaying for pSMAD1/5/8.
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3I and J

claim: Reduction of Bmp antagonists such as chordin is observed in Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos.
source: However, we see reduction of Bmp antagonists in these embryos, such as chordin, and thus additional studies are warranted to determine if Gdf3 is playing a direct or indirect role in modulating Bmp signaling in the early embryo.
evidence: Supported by RNA in situ hybridization shown in Figure 3N–Q

claim: Additional studies are warranted to determine if Gdf3 is playing a direct or indirect role in modulating Bmp signaling in the early embryo.
source: However, we see reduction of Bmp antagonists in these embryos, such as chordin, and thus additional studies are warranted to determine if Gdf3 is playing a direct or indirect role in modulating Bmp signaling in the early embryo.
evidence: Acknowledgment of uncertainty about mechanism

claim: Knockdown of Gdf3 can affect L-R patterning at two crucial steps: in formation of the L-R coordinator KV and in promoting robust expression of Nodal/Spaw in the LPM.
source: We demonstrate that knockdown of Gdf3 can affect L-R patterning at two crucial steps: in formation of the L-R coordinator KV and in promoting robust expression of Nodal/Spaw in the LPM.
evidence: Conclusion based on morpholino knockdown experiments

claim: Correct expression of sox17 is required for KV to form properly.
source: For KV to form properly, correct expression of sox17 is required (Aamar and Dawid, 2010), which itself requires robust Nodal signaling during germ layer formation (Sako et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Aamar and Dawid, 2010 and Sako et al., 2016

claim: Regional cell shape differences in KV depend on the presence of the neighboring notochord.
source: Furthermore, regional cell shape differences in KV depend on the presence of the neighboring notochord (Compagnon et al., 2014) which is absent in Nodal-signaling deficient embryos (Feldman et al., 1998).
evidence: Supported by citations to Compagnon et al., 2014 and Feldman et al., 1998

claim: In Gdf3 knockdown experiments, KV fails to acquire the regional cell shape differences that promote correct fluid flow.
source: In our Gdf3 knockdown experiments, KV fails to acquire the regional cell shape differences that promote correct fluid flow, which is required for proper asymmetric expression of dand5 (Figure 6C and D) (Schweickert et al., 2010; Lopes et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4B and model in Figure 6C and D

claim: Knockdown of Gdf3 prevents spaw expression from occurring in the LPM even in the absence of Nodal inhibitors Dand5 and Lefty1.
source: In addition to this phenotype, knockdown of Gdf3 also prevents spaw expression from occurring in the LPM even in the absence of Nodal inhibitors Dand5 and Lefty1 (Figure 6E).
evidence: Supported by double morpholino knockdown experiments shown in Figure 4D and model in Figure 6E

claim: Gdf3 plays a role both in KV organization and downstream, in the activation of LPM spaw.
source: These knockdown experiments suggest that Gdf3 plays a role both in KV organization and downstream, in the activation of LPM spaw.
evidence: Conclusion based on morpholino knockdown experiments

claim: Maternal Gdf3 is responsible for proper L-R patterning.
source: However, given that our data suggest maternal Gdf3 is responsible for proper L-R patterning, we suggest the differences in our results reflect the amount by which maternal Gdf3 is reduced with the two different AUG morpholinos that were used.
evidence: Conclusion based on the phenotypes of Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 mutants and rescue experiments

claim: The presence of zygotic gdf3 improved the rescue of L-R patterning defects in mesendoderm-rescued mutants.
source: Importantly, we demonstrated that the presence of zygotic gdf3 improved the rescue of L-R patterning defects in mesendoderm-rescued mutants.
evidence: Supported by rescue experiments comparing Mgdf3 and MZgdf3 embryos

claim: The lack of L-R patterning phenotypes in Zgdf3 mutants was unexpected.
source: The lack of L-R patterning phenotypes in Zgdf3 mutants was unexpected, especially since gdf3 is zygotically expressed in very strict domains that also express crucial L-R patterning genes such as the KV region and the LPM.
evidence: Authors' statement of expectation vs. observation

claim: While maternal Gdf3 is sufficient for proper L-R patterning, zygotic expression provides robustness to the system.
source: It could be that while maternal Gdf3 is sufficient for proper L-R patterning, zygotic expression provides robustness to the system.
evidence: Speculation based on the improved rescue with zygotic gdf3 present

claim: In the conditions used to raise zebrafish in the laboratory, maternally supplied gdf3 is sufficient for L-R patterning.
source: In the conditions used to raise zebrafish in the laboratory, such as controlled temperature, abundant food, and lack of predators, maternally supplied gdf3 is sufficient for this process.
evidence: Speculation based on the lack of phenotype in Zgdf3 mutants under laboratory conditions

claim: In situations where lower levels of maternal product are supplied, zygotic Gdf3 might be required alongside maternal Gdf3 for robust L-R patterning.
source: However, in situations where lower levels of maternal product are supplied, zygotic Gdf3 might then be required alongside maternal Gdf3 for robust L-R patterning.
evidence: Speculation about potential role of zygotic gdf3 under different conditions

claim: Gdf3 acts permissively to promote robust Nodal signaling.
source: Our results demonstrate that Gdf3 acts permissively to promote robust Nodal signaling, and yet is spatially restricted to KV and LPM during L-R patterning.
evidence: Conclusion based on the overall experimental results

claim: gdf3 is spatially restricted to KV and LPM during L-R patterning.
source: Our results demonstrate that Gdf3 acts permissively to promote robust Nodal signaling, and yet is spatially restricted to KV and LPM during L-R patterning.
evidence: Supported by expression pattern shown in Figure 1A

claim: gdf3 expression could be restricted to KV and LPM domains by similar patterning mechanisms as other L-R patterning components, even if spatial restriction of its expression is not required.
source: Given that other L-R patterning components are expressed in these distinct domains at this time, gdf3 expression could be restricted to these same domains by similar patterning mechanisms, even if spatial restriction of its expression is not required.
evidence: Speculation about the mechanism of gdf3 spatial restriction

claim: Gdf3 and Spaw dimerize to promote robust Nodal signaling in the LPM.
source: Taken together, we propose that Gdf3 and Spaw dimerize to promote robust Nodal signaling in the LPM.
evidence: Proposed model based on the experimental results

claim: Dimerization of Gdf3 and Spaw might allow Spaw to more efficiently travel to, and propagate through the LPM.
source: In the future, it will be interesting to see if dimerization of these ligands allows Spaw to more efficiently travel to, and propagate through the LPM.
evidence: Speculation about potential mechanism

claim: Gdf3 functions in multiple developmental processes.
source: Collectively, our data suggest that Gdf3 functions in multiple developmental processes.
evidence: Conclusion based on the multiple phenotypes observed at different developmental stages

claim: During the blastula and gastrula stages, Gdf3 affects Nodal activity required for organization of the vertebrate embryo as well as the formation of KV.
source: During the blastula and gastrula stages, Gdf3 affects Nodal activity required for organization of the vertebrate embryo as well as the formation of KV.
evidence: Conclusion based on the mesendoderm and KV defects in Mgdf3/MZgdf3 mutants

claim: During somitogenesis, Gdf3 is required for Nodal signaling in the LPM.
source: During somitogenesis it is required for Nodal signaling in the LPM.
evidence: Conclusion based on the loss of spaw expression in gdf3 morphants

claim: Mouse lines with targeted mutations in the Vg1 mouse orthologs Gdf1 and Gdf3 exhibited defects in mesoderm formation and L-R patterning.
source: This agrees with work performed in mouse, where lines with targeted mutations in the Vg1 mouse orthologs Gdf1 and Gdf3 exhibited defects in mesoderm formation and L-R patterning (Rankin et al., 2000; Andersson et al., 2006; 2007).
evidence: Supported by citations to Rankin et al., 2000 and Andersson et al., 2006; 2007

claim: Gdf3 functions as a co-ligand for Nodal signaling.
source: Our work also suggests that Gdf3 functions as a co-ligand for Nodal signaling.
evidence: Conclusion based on the requirement for Gdf3 to achieve robust Nodal signaling

claim: There is strong evidence that Vg1 orthologs can heterodimerize with Nodal to allow for robust or more efficient Nodal signaling.
source: Indeed, there is strong evidence that Vg1 orthologs can heterodimerize with Nodal to allow for robust or more efficient Nodal signaling (Tanaka et al., 2007; Fuerer et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Tanaka et al., 2007 and Fuerer et al., 2014

claim: Gdf3 facilitates Nodal ligands in generating a robust level of signaling activity required for both mesendoderm formation and proper L-R patterning.
source: Overall, we conclude that Gdf3 facilitates Nodal ligands in generating a robust level of signaling activity required for both mesendoderm formation and proper L-R patterning.

evidence: Established scientific knowledge

source: There are three Nodal orthologs in zebrafish; southpaw directs left-right asymmetries, while squint and cyclops function earlier to pattern mesendoderm.

claim: Gdf3 can affect left-right patterning at multiple stages, including proper development of regional cell morphology in Kupffer's vesicle.
source: We further show that Gdf3 can affect left-right patterning at multiple stages, including proper development of regional cell morphology in Kupffer's vesicle and the establishment of southpaw expression in the lateral plate mesoderm.
